applicability: Continuous admission, mixed prefill/decode and final drain
Recorded Drama3 B300 C64 diagnostic only
limitations: No new measurement or trace reproduction
Selected-phase occupancy is not service throughput
Raw evidence remains under its existing owner
attribution: InferRSI issue #10 diagnostic evidence; extraction retains the original observation and its limits

findings.direction: Split admitted traffic from the final drain when reading decode occupancy
findings.reason: Across the 256-request B300 diagnostic, pure decode averaged 60.718 of 64 active requests during admission, 8.793 in drain and 28.146 over the full trace. The trace-wide mean cannot identify how full decode was while requests were still entering.
findings.revisit_when: Mark the client admission interval and the final drain in the trace before using occupancy to select a scheduling hypothesis.
findings.bounds: Drama3 B300, 256 requests and a C64 continuous-admission diagnostic; approximate CPU/GPU clock alignment.

findings.direction: Count scheduler steps using owning CPU annotations
findings.reason: The owning CPU annotations count 1 prefill, 37 mixed, 762 decode and 2 empty steps, totaling 802. PIECEWISE fragments describe graph execution, and scheduled prompt entries may describe chunks.
findings.revisit_when: Verify annotation ownership, align the clocks and pair the counts with actual generated work when profiling another trace.

findings.direction: Carry the complete cohort into the service gate
findings.reason: Near-full decode occupancy in a selected interval is a diagnostic. The service decision still depends on all requests, complete quality and repetition groups, and the end-to-end metric.
findings.revisit_when: Use phase statistics to pick a hypothesis. Evaluate the resulting change with the unchanged complete cohort and matched frozen service controls.
